prompts.dev1: Hey, I see sales dropping on our app. Ines says we need more inventory checks right now.
prompts.dev2: Oh no, someone wants a fix but I don't know if it will help or hurt us.

answers.text: Let's change everything immediately to please them even if the data looks bad.
answers.feedback: This destroys trust and wastes effort by ignoring what the evidence shows.

answers.text: Maybe we should just add a feature if the stakeholder insists on it.
answers.feedback: Ignoring the numbers risks building something useless that wastes our time.

answers.text: Check the last three months' sales data first before changing anything.
answers.feedback: This follows evidence instead of guessing. It keeps decisions safe and smart.

prompts.dev1: I think we should just cancel this sprint since the checkout feature is completely broken right now.
prompts.dev2: But I am so worried that if we stop, everyone will be mad and miss their deadline.

answers.text: Keep the Sprint Goal fixed and remove only the one blocker to keep moving forward.
answers.feedback: This focuses on solving the problem without losing the team's overall purpose or direction.

answers.feedback: Abandoning the goal removes focus and causes the team to work on nothing important together.

answers.text: We could split this into two sprints, doing part of checkout now and the rest later.
answers.feedback: Splitting the goal breaks its single nature and may confuse everyone about what they are building.

answers.feedback: This stops inspection and adaptation by hiding problems until it is too late.
